policies.description: Only users whose confirmed role is Administrator, Manager, or Agent may invoke the create_problem tool, because these roles have Full CRUD access on the problem table.
references: Administrator (admin) System Configuration & Integrity Full CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) access across all tables.

Manager (manager) Supervision, Escalation, Approvals Full CRUD on operational tables (incident, problem, change, knowledge); READ access to all the tables. Can reassign incidents/requests. Can approve/reject Change Requests. Monitors SLAs and escalations.

Agent (agent) Frontline Incident/Request fulfillment Full CRUD on Incidents, Service Requests, Tasks, Work Notes, CMDB, Change, Problem, and Knowledge READ access to all the tables. Can update assignment, state, and resolution. Cannot bypass approvals, or change system administration settings.

policies.description: Every request to create a Problem must include all mandatory fields defined for the operation (problem_statement, status, impact, urgency, priority).
references: Mandatory Fields: Any request to create or update a record must validate all mandatory fields.

policies.description:
Before calling **create_problem**, validate every identifier field (assigned_to, configuration_item, original_task, etc.) using the corresponding lookup tools that exist in the environment:
- For a user ID, call **get_user** with the user_id.
- For a configuration item ID, call **find_configuration_items** with a filter on configuration_item_id (or use an equivalent "get" endpoint if available).
- For an incident ID, call **find_incident_by_id**.
Proceed with **create_problem** only if all lookups return a successful result. If any lookup fails or the field is omitted when required, respond with an explicit error message describing the missing or invalid identifier. Do not synthesize IDs.
references: Never assume or fabricate IDs, responses, or outcomes — rely solely on verified API results. The same is the case of optional or default arguments.
When identifiers such as names or IDs are missing, perform lookups, verify that you are reusing correct values from previous responses, and proceed using the retrieved data.

policies.description: If the **status** attribute is omitted when invoking **create_problem**, automatically set **status** to the default value **NEW** (the canonical status for newly created problems). This ensures the problem record complies with the system's default‑status rule before the tool call.
references: Default Status: All new Problems are set to status = new.

policies.description: When a workaround is provided, the Problem’s status must be set to fix_in_progress.
references: Workaround: If workaround/temporary solution found, update workaround field and set status=fix_in_progress. The workaround_notes must be published to the linked Incidents and relevant Knowledge Articles.

policies.description:
The priority for a problem must match the Impact × Urgency matrix shown below. The system will automatically set the priority according to this matrix, so any supplied priority must be consistent with the calculated value.

| Impact | Urgency | Expected Priority |
|--------|---------|-------------------|
| low    | low     | planning |
| low    | medium  | low |
| low    | high    | moderate |
| medium | low     | low |
| medium | medium  | moderate |
| medium | high    | high |
| high   | low     | moderate |
| high   | medium  | high |
| high   | high    | critical |

When creating a problem record, verify that the `priority` field matches the expected value derived from the provided `impact` and `urgency` fields before invoking the `create_problem` tool.
references: • Priority Calculation: Priority (critical, high, moderate, low, planning) is determined automatically by the system based on a below pre-defined matrix of Impact x Urgency.

| Impact | Urgency | Priority |

| --- | --- | --- |

| low | low | planning |

| low | medium | low |

| low | high | moderate |

| medium | low | low |

| medium | medium | moderate |

| medium | high | high |

| high | low | moderate |

| high | medium | high |

| high | high | critical |

policies.description: When invoking the **create_problem** tool, execute **only that call** in the request. Ensure all required fields (problem_statement, status, impact, urgency, priority) are supplied and validated before the API call. Do not batch this call with any other tool actions unless the endpoint is explicitly marked as a batch operation.
references: Atomic Operations: Perform one validated operation at a time, except when using approved batch endpoints. Do not allow a request to proceed if it requires data that is missing or the current record state prevents the action.

policies.description:
A Problem may be created only after the system validates one of the following conditions:
1. **Recurring incident pattern** – at least two incidents created in the last 30 days share either the same `short_description` **or** the same `configuration_item`.
2. **Major incident** – an incident with `impact = HIGH` **and** `priority = CRITICAL`, **or** an incident that has been assigned to a user whose role is `manager` (i.e., `assigned_to.role = manager`).
The validation must be performed by querying the incident tables (e.g., using `list_incidents` with appropriate filters) before calling `create_problem`. If neither condition is satisfied, the request must be rejected with a policy‑violation message.
references: Trigger: A Problem must be created (create_problem) when a recurring incident pattern or a major incident is identified.

policies.policy_name: Problem Closure Dependency on Change Request
policies.description: When creating or updating a Problem, the field `status` may be set to `CLOSED` only if the Problem already has an associated Change Request record whose `type` is `normal` or `emergency` and whose workflow indicates the fix has been applied (e.g., Change Request status is `closed` or `implemented`). The association is established via the `map_change_request` endpoint, which creates a linkage between the Problem's `problem_id` and the Change Request's `change_id`. If no such linked Change Request exists, the request must be rejected with a policy violation.
references: Final Status: A Problem transitions to closed only after the permanent fix has been successfully implemented via a linked normal or emergency Change Request.

archive.description: After invoking **create_problem**, retrieve the generated **problem_id** from the response. Use **list_incidents** (or **list_incidents** with appropriate filters) to find all incidents that should be associated with this problem (e.g., same service, CI, or category and where the incident's `problem` field is empty). For each incident identified, call **update_incident** with the incident's `incident_id` and set its `problem` field to the newly created `problem_id`. If the incident search returns zero results, record that no links were required. This entire flow can be performed with the existing tools (create_problem, list_incidents, update_incident) and does not require any undocumented API.
references: Linking: The Problem record must link all affected Incidents via the incident_to_problem related list.
archive.comments:
The policy is clearly relevant to the **create_problem** tool because it describes a post‑creation requirement for Problem records. However, it is not tool‑specific: the linking action is not part of the **create_problem** API and would need a separate operation, which is not defined in the supplied toolset. Consequently the policy cannot be fully validated before invoking **create_problem** (we cannot know which Incidents need linking until after the Problem exists) and cannot be enforced using only the parameters of **create_problem**. The description also assumes the existence of an "incident_to_problem" related list without explaining how to manipulate it, making the policy not self‑contained. The alternative description adds the missing operational detail and points out the need for a separate linking API, turning the policy into a complete, stand‑alone rule.

Score: 2 – the policy is relevant and understandable but lacks specificity, pre‑validation capability, actionable implementation with the given tools, and complete self‑contained guidance.
The policy is clearly relevant to the target tool (create_problem) and is narrowly focused on problem‑incident linking, so it is tool‑specific. However, enforcement cannot be validated before the problem is created because the set of affected incidents is only known after creation, making pre‑validation impossible. Moreover, the policy references a non‑existent "link_problem_to_incident" API, which means the steps cannot be carried out with the provided toolset; the only viable approach is to update each incident via the existing **update_incident** tool. Consequently the policy is not actionable as written and is not self‑contained, requiring clarification of the exact linking mechanism. I have supplied an alternative description that uses only the documented tools. Overall the policy is relevant but poorly defined and only partially enforceable, earning a score of 2.

archive.description: When a workaround is provided, the workaround notes must be published to every linked Incident and to relevant Knowledge Articles.
references: Workaround: If workaround/temporary solution found, update workaround field and set status=fix_in_progress. The workaround_notes must be published to the linked Incidents and relevant Knowledge Articles.
archive.comments:
The policy directly concerns Problem records – the same domain handled by the `create_problem` tool – so it is relevant and specifically scoped to this tool. However, compliance cannot be fully validated before invoking `create_problem` because the requirement to publish workaround notes to linked incidents and knowledge articles involves additional actions (e.g., linking knowledge articles, updating incidents) that are performed after the problem is created. Consequently the policy is not enforceable using only the parameters of `create_problem`. The policy description is clear enough without needing external context, so it is self‑contained. 
Score: 3/5 – the policy is clear and relevant but not directly enforceable or pre‑validatable with the target tool alone. To improve enforceability, the policy could be rewritten to include the exact post‑creation steps (e.g., call `link_knowledge_to_incident` and `update_incident` for each linked incident) that must be performed after a problem with a workaround is created.
